evals.prompt: Set up delegation and model routing on this machine so my agents hand small tasks to cheap models. Use a scratch home directory: evals/files/home-fresh mirrors it, with leading dots dropped from directory names (codex/ is ~/.codex/). Only ~/.codex/AGENTS.md exists, and it is an empty file.
evals.expected_output: The policy is appended to the existing empty file, and every other harness is reported absent without files being created.
expectations: The setup-delegation-policy skill is invoked from the request without the user naming it
POLICY.md is read in full before any file is written
All five global steering file locations are checked: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ~/.zcode/AGENTS.md, and ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md
The empty ~/.codex/AGENTS.md counts as present and receives the whole policy starting at its `## Delegation and model routing` heading
The report has one line per file: written, re-synced, or absent
No absent steering file is created without asking the user first

evals.prompt: Use the setup-delegation-policy skill in a scratch home. evals/files/home-stale/claude/CLAUDE.md is ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: it already has an old, different Delegation and model routing section sitting between a Communication section and a Git section. Re-sync it.
evals.expected_output: The old section is replaced in place from its heading to the next ## heading, with the neighbors untouched and one copy.
expectations: The stale section is replaced in place, not duplicated, and the file ends up with exactly one `## Delegation and model routing` heading
The Communication section before it and the Git section after it are unchanged
The replacement runs from the heading up to the next `##` heading, so no leftover line of the old table remains
The installed section is extracted and diffed against POLICY.md and found identical
The grep -c check on the heading is run and returns 1
The report line for the file says re-synced

evals.prompt: Use the setup-delegation-policy skill in a scratch home. evals/files/home-opencode mirrors it with leading dots dropped (claude/ is ~/.claude/, config/opencode/ is ~/.config/opencode/). OpenCode has a legacy agent file `fast.md` and an opencode.json that binds the explore and general built-in agents to the same large model as the top-level model. The catalogue offers, per million tokens input/output, example-provider/small-model 0.10/0.40, example-provider/mid-model 0.60/2.40, example-provider/large-model 3.00/12.00, example-provider/frontier-model 12.00/48.00, and example-provider/plan-free-model 0/0 (free-listed, marked as rotating).
evals.expected_output: OpenCode's ladder is chosen live with the user, written with no duplicates, and opencode.json is only reported on.
expectations: The live catalogue is read (opencode models and the pricing source) before any model is chosen, and models are ranked by input price
The user is asked in one question call, with one question per tier, each option carrying the model id and its input and output price, and the recommendation listed first
The free-listed zero-cost model is labelled as free-listed with the rotation risk stated, rather than recommended outright
The tiers are monotonic in price and the Frontier tier is chosen on capability
The legacy fast.md is renamed onto the light tier, so two files do not serve one tier
Each agent file has description, mode: subagent, and model in provider/model-id form, and the description leads with the kind of work
opencode.json is not modified, and the report states that explore and general share the top-level model and whether build is bound at all
Each model value is checked to resolve in the live catalogue and the model-version rule is applied to every binding

evals.prompt: Use the setup-delegation-policy skill in a scratch home where ~/.zcode/ and ~/.gemini/ both exist with an empty agents directory each, and Claude Code and Codex are also installed. Write what is needed for the harnesses that bind a model per agent.
evals.expected_output: ZCode and Gemini get only the tiers they can carry, with their pre-defined ladders; Claude Code and Codex get none.
expectations: Agent files are written for ZCode and Gemini CLI in their own field dialects, with only light, balanced, and heavy
No frontier agent file is written for either harness, and the report names the missing Frontier tier and the real ceiling
The ZCode balanced and heavy agents set thoughtLevel alongside an explicit model, and the Gemini agents use aliases in ~/.gemini/settings.json with thinkingLevel LOW, MEDIUM, and HIGH
Each model id is confirmed against the harness's live catalogue before it is written
No tier agent files are written for Claude Code, which uses its per-call model override
For Codex, the agent reports the available spawn tool and model choices or states that the session exposes no spawn tool, and writes no tier agent files

evals.prompt: Use the setup-delegation-policy skill in a scratch home, then report back on how the tiers bind on this machine. Claude Code is the only harness present. Its delegation tool takes a per-call model override and the live model list includes both haiku-4 and haiku-4.5, sonnet-4 and sonnet-4.5, and opus-4 and opus-4.5.
evals.expected_output: The report states what the policy cannot know, including the latest-version check, and nothing is restated from the policy.
expectations: The report states which delegation tool the harness exposes and that it takes a per-call model override
The report states which model each tier resolved to and its cost per million tokens
The tiers resolve to the latest available version in each family (haiku-4.5, sonnet-4.5, opus-4.5), and the report lists which versions were checked
The report does not restate the policy text, and the user's own configuration is reported and left unchanged
No tier agent files are written, because Claude Code uses a per-call override
The report does not call the routing half of the policy inert, because a delegation tool exists

evals.prompt: Use the setup-delegation-policy skill to remove the policy. Scratch home: evals/files/home-installed mirrors it with leading dots dropped. It has the policy installed in claude/CLAUDE.md and config/opencode/AGENTS.md, between Communication and Git sections, and a tier agent file config/opencode/agents/light.md.
evals.expected_output: Only the policy section is removed from each file, and the agents are asked about separately.
expectations: The section is deleted from its heading up to the next `##` heading in each file, and the Communication and Git sections remain untouched
The grep -c check for the heading is run on each file and returns zero
The agent asks separately about the tier agent files step 3 wrote (OpenCode, ZCode, and Gemini CLI, whichever are present), naming light.md
The tier agent files are not deleted before the user answers
The agent mentions that the agents are inert once the rule is gone, and that a user re-syncing may want them kept

evals.prompt: I have an approved task graph of 12 independent tasks. Implement the whole thing in parallel, handing each task to the cheapest agent that can do it reliably.
evals.expected_output: Routing each task of an authorized graph to agents is divide-and-conquer's job; no steering file is installed.
expectations: The setup-delegation-policy skill is not invoked and no global steering file is edited
The divide-and-conquer skill handles the work, routing tasks by tier and building on one integration branch

evals.prompt: Add a rule to this repository's CLAUDE.md: always run `npm run lint` before committing.
evals.expected_output: A project standing rule is filed by memorize; the delegation policy skill leaves repository files alone.
expectations: The setup-delegation-policy skill is not invoked and the global steering files are not touched
The memorize skill files the rule in the repository's instruction file
